title: Platform adoption workstream alignment - AtlasStream onboarding
summary: Kickoff alignment to sequence AtlasStream's Redwood onboarding into three parallel workstreams: infra/provisioning, model & integration, and adoption/training. Agreement on a 6-week pilot window with clear acceptance criteria around latency, cost per 1k tokens, and key accuracy checks. Action items: Redwood to share runbook, SOW draft, and a security pack; AtlasStream to provide sample dataset access and org SSO admin contact.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-30 15:00 PDT · 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Mike Alvarez (CTO, AtlasStream), Priyanka Rao (Head of ML), Omar Siddiqui (Infra), Sara Linton (Product), Tom Brewer (Data Eng)

[00:00] Jordan: okay hi everyone thanks for hopping on, we're gonna run through the adoption workstreams, make sure folks know owners and timeline. quick note, recording is on.
[00:12] Mike: yeah thanks Jordan, excited to get this moving. we have a big Q4 push to get gen-ai features into the product.
[00:18] Priyanka: hi, I'm Priyanka, we own the model evaluation and will be responsible for quality gates.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood): great, thanks Priyanka. we'll align on the eval harness we usually use — small prompt set + regen testing — and we can drop the template into your repo.
[00:38] Omar: quick infra note, we need VPC peering details and whether you support our private deployment pattern. last time I checked there was Redwood Private with customer-managed VPC, is that right?
[00:48] Jordan: correct — Redwood Private supports VPC peering and on-prem packaging. two deployment paths for the pilot: hosted with strict data retention policies, or Private in your VPC. we should decide by next week because provisioning times differ.
[01:02] Sara: timeline wise, what's realistic? we want a pilot up in six weeks.
[01:08] Lena (CSM): six weeks is doable if we parallelize infra and model integration. week 1-2: infra & auth; week 2-4: model integration + sample traffic; week 4-6: evaluation & acceptance.
[01:20] Tom: on data access, we'll need a secure mechanism to upload sanitized sample logs. do you have an S3 signed upload flow or a direct sftp?
[01:30] Priya (Redwood): we typically do an S3 signed URL + limited lifetime, or you can place data in a restricted bucket and give us a role. we also can accept encrypted bundles via your KMS.
[01:40] Mike: security is big for us. SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs — will Redwood provide evidence and architecture docs?
[01:48] Jordan: yes — we'll share the security pack (SOC2 summary, SAML setup guide, logging/audit docs). we'll also include KMS integration notes for envelope encryption.
[02:00] Priyanka: on acceptance criteria, we care about latency P95 under load, cost per 1k tokens compared to our current baseline, and specific accuracy thresholds on our evaluation set.
[02:12] Priya (Redwood): sounds good — our Console can show token-level cost and per-route latency breakdowns. we'll configure a route for the pilot and wire up the dashboards.
[02:23] Omar: instrumenting traces — can we ship X-Ray/Jaeger spans? we want correlation in our APM.
[02:30] Priya (Redwood): yes we emit trace hooks; integration is usually via a tracing endpoint we provide. we can demo that in the technical deep dive.
[02:40] Mike: any blockers on compliance? do you do customer-managed keys?
[02:45] Jordan: yes we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated. hosted can also be configured with CMK for enterprise accounts.
[02:56] Sara: training — who will run the enablement for product and support teams?
[03:00] Lena (CSM): Lena will run a two-part enablement: product workshop (1 hour) and ops/infra runbook walkthrough (90 minutes). we'll record sessions and drop materials in the onboarding folder.
[03:14] Tom: demo cadence — can we do a live integration review in two weeks?
[03:18] Jordan: yes, Jordan to schedule a technical deep dive with Priya and your infra folks. expect an invite for Oct 14th or 15th.
[03:27] 
[03:30] -- Transcript jump to integration specifics --
[03:31] Priya (Redwood): for the model, do you plan to use an open checkpoint hosted by us or bring your own?
[03:36] Priyanka: we want to start with an open LLM for comparison and then test a finetuned variant. we'll need to version the model and be able to rollback.
[03:45] Priya (Redwood): rollouts and pins are supported — we can do canary deploys and automatic fallback to a smaller / quantized variant if compute gets constrained.
[03:53] Mike: what about batching — P95 latency is important, but we also need cost controls. how do you balance that?
[03:59] Priya (Redwood): Redwood Optimize will recommend batching and quantization profiles per workload. you can set an SLO for latency and a cost ceiling; the routing policy can favor cheaper variants outside of peak latency-sensitive routes.
[04:15] Omar: networking question — for private we need to open ports to a specific subnet; do you have an infra checklist?
[04:22] Jordan: yes, we'll share a provisioning checklist with exact CIDR ranges, firewall rules, and expected provisioning windows.
[04:30] 
[04:32] -- Objections and tradeoffs --
[04:33] Priyanka: one concern — our regulatory team wants data to never leave the EU. do you support region-pin for hosted?
[04:40] Jordan: yes, hosted model routing can be pinned to EU regions and Dedicated can be placed in a region of your choice. for strict residency the Private option is recommended.
[04:50] Mike: cost — how predictable is the billing during pilot? we'd prefer a capped pilot budget.
[04:57] Jordan: we can offer a pilot credit model or a short-term reserved capacity for the window. I'll propose options in the SOW.
[05:08] Sara: who signs off on acceptance? Product or ML?
[05:12] Priyanka: ML will own the accuracy gate, Product will sign off on UX and latency.
[05:18] Lena (CSM): we'll document acceptance criteria and add them to the SOW so signoff is explicit.
[05:25] 
[05:27] -- Near the end, recap & next steps --
[05:28] Jordan: recap: Redwood shares runbook + security pack + SOW draft; AtlasStream shares sanitized sample dataset and SSO admin contact; schedule tech deep dive for mid-Oct; Lena to set enablement dates.
[05:42] Mike: sounds good. can you also include an example pricing scenario for Dedicated vs hosted?
[05:48] Jordan: yes, I'll include a short comparison and expected unit economics for your traffic profile.
[05:53] Priyanka: one small ask — include the eval harness template and a sample prompt set we can start with.
[05:58] Priya (Redwood): will do.
[06:00] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts in 48 hours.
[06:04] Mike: thanks team. bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional overlap, some product names transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" or "Redwood Private" inconsistently, which is present in this transcript.
